title: Relational Mediators: LLM Chatbots as Boundary Objects in Psychotherapy

bias_targets.target: Sexual orientation and gender identity bias
bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative semi-structured interviews and scenario-based evaluations using speculative design probes with LGBTQ+ clients and therapists. The study assesses experiences of provider bias, societal stigma, and the "educator burden" in therapy, exploring how LLM chatbots can mediate identity conflicts and relational safety.

Qualitative interviews and design probes evaluating how LLMs can address cultural misalignments, specifically examining the tension between Western-centric therapeutic frameworks and Chinese cultural contexts, and evaluating the need for culturally sensitive, community-validated AI dialogue.

In-depth interviews with economically dependent and disadvantaged clients to explore structural inequalities, institutional power asymmetries, and access barriers in mental healthcare, assessing how dynamic LLM features might redistribute relational power.
